# Inputs & Outputs

KM curve image (high resolution recommended; if curves strongly overlap, split into one image per arm).

Numbers-at-risk table with corresponding time points (strongly recommended; reconstruction is possible without it, but accuracy degrades).

Total sample size and total number of events (helps enforce integer constraints and interval balancing).

## Output

Individual-level table: time, status (1 = event, 0 = censored), group.
This reproduces KM, HR/CI, and supports Cox/RMST/parametric survival modeling and NMA.

# Digitization

Read JPG/PNG -> convert to HSL color space

Detect x/y axes and crop to plotting region

Remove background/text (lightness thresholding and optional OCR)

Cluster by color to separate multiple curves (set expected number of curves)

Repair overlaps/missing pixels

Extract curve pixel trajectories

Map pixel coordinates back to real time and survival scales

Output a structured data frame (curve_id, time, survival)

# Step 2: Preprocessing

For each arm’s $(t,\hat{S})$:

Add origin: if the first point is not $(0,1)$, insert $(0,1)$.

Enforce monotonicity: if $\hat{S}(t_j)>\hat{S}(t_{j-1})$, truncate to $\hat{S}(t_j)\leftarrow\hat{S}(t_{j-1})$.

Align intervals: segment by numbers-at-risk time points (if available).

Numeric guards: rounding and de-duplication to avoid negative counts, etc.

Rule of thumb: preprocessing + risk table are accuracy multipliers; without them, HR/CI agreement often degrades.

# Collect & align the numbers-at-risk

Prepare the set ${(t_i^{\text{risk}},,n_i^{\text{risk}})}$ and align times to the curve times (decimal harmonization or nearest-neighbor matching).

Check ordering/consistency: start, total $N$, tail at-risk vs. total events balance.

Without the risk table, reconstruction is possible but HR/CI robustness declines; use with caution for high-stakes conclusions.

# Restruction, methodology and formula

Digitized coordinates: ${(t_k,\hat{S}k)}{k=1}^{K}$ (monotone in $\hat{S}$).

Risk table: ${(t_i^{\text{risk}},,n_i^{\text{risk}})}_{i=1}^{T}$.

Segment ${(t_k,\hat{S}k)}$ into intervals $[,t_i^{\text{risk}},,t{i+1}^{\text{risk}})$.

KM update at event time $j$: $S_j = S_{j-1}!\left(1-\dfrac{d_j}{n_j}\right)$

Implied events: $\hat{d}j \approx n_j!\left(1-\dfrac{S_j}{S{j-1}}\right)$, with $0\le \hat{d}_j \le n_j$

$\hat{c}_i \;=\; n_i^{\text{risk}}$

$\sum_{t_k \in [\,t_i^{\text{risk}},\,t_{i+1}^{\text{risk}}\,)} \hat{d}_k$

$n_{i+1}^{\text{risk}} $

$\hat{c}_i \;=\; n_i^{\text{risk}} \cdot \frac{S_{\text{after}}}{S_{\text{before}}}$

$t^{\text{cens}}_{i,m} \sim \text{Uniform}\!\bigl(t_i^{\text{risk}},\,t_{i+1}^{\text{risk}}\bigr)$

$t^{\text{cens}}_{i,m} \text{ evenly spaced in } [t_i^{\text{risk}},\,t_{i+1}^{\text{risk}}).$

# Generate IPD

For each event time $t_k$: assign $\hat{d}_k$ subjects an event at $t_k$.

For each interval: assign $\hat{c}i$ subjects censoring uniformly (or evenly) in $[,t_i^{\text{risk}},,t{i+1}^{\text{risk}})$.

Iterate through intervals; any remaining at risk at the end are censored in a short tail window.

# Quality control (QC) & consistency

Redraw KM from reconstructed IPD and overlay with digitized/adjusted curve (or original figure).

Metrics

On $[0,t_{\max}]$ with 100 equally spaced checkpoints, using right-continuous remapping, compute RMSE/MAE/max error and KS.

Fit Cox with group as the only covariate; compare reconstructed HR/CI with published values; report absolute % HR difference and CI non-overlap.

Empirical baseline

Typical multi-study results: mean absolute HR difference $\approx 2\text{–}3%$, median $\approx 2%$, most $<5%$. If much larger, inspect image quality and risk table first.

# Common failure modes & fixes

Low resolution / heavy overlap / dense censor ticks → use higher-quality images; split per arm; tune denoising or assist semi-manually.

Missing preprocessing (origin/monotonicity) → may cause non-convergence or large HR bias; always preprocess.

Missing risk table → larger HR/CI discrepancies; avoid for high-stakes conclusions.

PH violations (e.g., crossing hazards) → don’t rely on constant HR/log-rank; use RMST or time-varying HR.
